pattern: Ingest → normalise → group → rank → serve: a streaming pipeline turns many noisy sources into a few precomputed, shared lists, and the request path only blends cached candidates for the reader.

checks.label: Where the content comes from captured

tips.nudge: You write no articles yourself. Where does everything on the page come from?
tips.hint: Write a functional requirement for collecting articles from publishers.
tips.show: F1: Continuously collect new articles (title, snippet, image, URL) from ~50k publishers' feeds and sitemaps.

tips.nudge: Two hundred outlets write about the same earthquake. How many cards does the reader see?
tips.hint: Add a requirement about how coverage of the same event is presented.
tips.show: F2: Articles about the same event are grouped into one story with a 'full coverage' list; near-identical copies are removed.

tips.nudge: Is the home page the same for a sports fan and a markets trader?
tips.hint: Add a requirement for a page section that depends on the reader.
tips.show: F4: Logged-in readers get a 'For you' section built from followed topics and reading history.

checks.label: How quickly new stories must appear

tips.nudge: A big story breaks. How long can it take to show up?
tips.hint: State a freshness target from publication to the home page.
tips.show: N2: A breaking story appears within ~5 minutes of first publication.

tips.nudge: Start from new articles per day.
tips.hint: articles/day ÷ seconds in a day.
tips.show: 2M / day ≈ 23 /s (peaks ~100 /s on big news days).

tips.nudge: How many requests do you make to publishers to find those articles?
tips.hint: sources ÷ average poll interval.
tips.show: 50k sources / 300 s ≈ 170 feed fetches /s.

tips.nudge: Readers × page views, then the breaking-news spike.
tips.hint: Convert daily page views to per second and apply the spike factor.
tips.show: 100M × 5 = 500M views/day ≈ 5.8k /s; ×5 on breaking news ≈ 29k /s.

tips.nudge: You keep metadata, not whole pages. How big is a year of it?
tips.hint: articles/year × bytes per article record.
tips.show: 2M × 365 × 5 KB ≈ 3.7 TB/year of article metadata (+ ~1 TB of 30-day text for clustering).

tips.nudge: What does the app call to draw the home page?
tips.hint: A GET for an edition's top stories, plus one for the personal section.
tips.show: GET /stories?edition=en-US&topic=&cursor= → {stories[{story_id, headline, articles[3], coverage_count}]}; GET /for-you.

tips.nudge: What do you keep about each article you found?
tips.hint: One record per canonical URL, with what you need to cluster and display it.
tips.show: articles(article_id, canonical_url, source_id, title, snippet, image_url, published_at, simhash, embedding, story_id).

tips.nudge: What do you show as one card on the home page?
tips.hint: An entity that groups articles and carries ranking signals.
tips.show: stories(story_id, headline, centroid, article_ids, first_seen, last_updated, coverage_count, topic, editions).

checks.label: Collecting articles designed as its own part

tips.nudge: 50k publishers, each publishing at its own pace. How do you notice a new article within minutes without hammering them?
tips.hint: Add a part for ingestion: compare fixed polling, adaptive polling and push, and draw scheduler, fetchers and a buffer.
tips.show: Part 'Ingestion': a scheduler adapts each source's poll interval and accepts WebSub pings; fetchers do conditional GETs and put new articles on a stream.

checks.label: Grouping coverage designed as its own part

tips.nudge: Syndicated copies are near-identical; different outlets' takes are similar but not the same. Two problems?
tips.hint: Add a part for dedup and clustering: exact vs near-duplicate detection, batch vs incremental clustering.
tips.show: Part 'Dedup and clustering': canonical URL + SimHash drop copies; each unique article joins the nearest recent story centroid (embeddings) or starts a new story; periodic batch re-clustering merges and splits.

checks.label: Ordering stories designed as its own part

tips.nudge: Which of today's 50k stories goes first, and for whom?
tips.hint: Add a part for ranking: global vs per-user, computed at request time or ahead of time.
tips.show: Part 'Ranking and personalisation': a ranker scores stories every minute (freshness, coverage, source authority) into lists per edition/topic; the request re-ranks a few hundred candidates with the reader's interest profile.

checks.label: Read path designed as its own part

tips.nudge: A breaking story multiplies traffic by five within minutes. What answers those requests?
tips.hint: Add a part for serving: what is cached where, and what must be computed per reader.
tips.show: Part 'Serving': anonymous edition pages cached at the CDN for ~30 s; personalised sections blended by stateless API servers from cached candidate lists.

checks.label: Read path can absorb breaking-news spikes

tips.nudge: Everyone in a country sees almost the same top stories. How often should you compute that page?
tips.hint: Put something in front that serves the shared parts without recomputing.
tips.show: CDN caching edition pages for ~30 s + Redis holding ranked story lists per edition/topic.

tips.nudge: Tens of thousands of requests per second on a big news day.
tips.hint: Stateless API servers behind something that distributes requests.
tips.show: CDN → load balancer → stateless news API servers.

tips.nudge: Fetchers are fast; clustering is slow and bursty. Should they wait on each other?
tips.hint: Put a buffer between the crawl side and the processing side.
tips.show: Fetchers → raw-articles stream (Kafka) → dedup/extract workers.

checks.label: How often each source is checked decided

tips.nudge: A wire service publishes every minute; a local blog once a week. Same interval?
tips.hint: Decide how a source's poll interval is set and changed, and how push fits in.
tips.show: Adaptive interval per source (shrink when new items appear, grow when not, 1–60 min), WebSub push where supported, per-host politeness limits.

tips.nudge: The clusterer falls behind on a huge news day. What does the reader see?
tips.hint: Go stage by stage: what is buffered, what degrades, what is served stale.
tips.show: Stream buffers raw articles; pages serve the last ranked lists (stale but up); fetchers back off failing hosts; clustering lag shows as singleton stories, merged later.

tips.nudge: How would you know a breaking story is late?
tips.hint: List metrics for each stage from publish to page.
tips.show: Publish → visible latency per source, fetch error rate, stream lag, cluster size distribution, page p99, CDN hit ratio.
